The branch made three behaviour changes. All are fixed in the working tree on `refactor/modules`, and nothing is committed yet.

1. **`src/lineItems.js` (commit bf8194c, `assertInt`)**: `assertInt(qty, 0, …)` started accepting `qty: 0`, where `main` required at least 1. I changed the minimum back to 1.
2. **`src/discount.js` (commit ccfc250, "Rename locals")**: the rewrite merged two checks into `if (!code || !entry) return 0`, so an unknown discount code returned 0 instead of throwing `unknown code: …`. I restored the original order: no code returns 0, an unknown code throws. The new variable names stay.
3. **`src/currency.js` (commit 4376a4e)**: the exchange-rate refresh changes every converted amount, so it doesn't belong on a pure refactor. I undid it with `git revert --no-commit 4376a4e`. If you want the new rates, they should go in their own PR.

To check for anything else, I diffed `src` against `main` with quote and semicolon differences stripped out. Everything left is the file split, renamed variables, the `assertInt` helper, and `function` changed to arrow functions. None of those change behaviour: no function is called before it's defined, and none uses `this` or `arguments`. Removing semicolons doesn't change how any line parses. The test files only changed import paths.

All 517 tests pass. I also ran the two restored cases by hand: `qty: 0` throws `bad qty for A` and code `NOPE` throws `unknown code: NOPE`. The tests didn't catch any of the three changes, so it may be worth adding tests for them.
